proves: a dashed border is drawn as dashes with the rhythm a browser draws, on a box no fixture drew before this one
checkable: 240x48 on white, one box filling it with `border: 4px dashed #000000`. Read the TOP band at row y=2, which is the middle of the 4-wide band, between x=40 and x=200 - forty pixels clear of each corner, because CSS Backgrounds 3 §4.4 divides a corner between its two edges and a run including one measures the join rather than the rhythm. A pixel counts as ink below 128 in the red channel. AND read a COLUMN as well, at x=100, clear of both corners: four inked rows then nothing. The row alone certified this image for as long as it was wrong vertically - `an accepted image carries far more than the measurement that certified it`, and the vertical reading is the half that was missing.
chrome: measured, not accepted from our own render: `on:5 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:5 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:5 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:8 off:4 on:6` - dash exactly 8 (twice the width), gaps of 4 with a 5 wherever the remainder falls. The first and last runs are cut by the window and are not whole periods. From `crates/meo-canvas/tests/assets/chrome/border-rhythm.tsv`. VERTICAL, re-measured by MC Main on 2026-08-24: sampled clear of the corners the top band is FOUR fully-inked rows - y=0, y=1, y=2 and y=3 all at alpha 1.000, and y=4 at 0.000. The image accepted before that date drew 3.5 rows: y=3 came out at roughly 0.44 because the corner division split the band lengthwise between two edges that agreed. The rhythm along x was right the whole time, which is why the run sequence above is unchanged.
chrome_at_the_corner: read from the box's own left edge outward, with the §4.4 division at offset 4: `on:8@0 off:4@8 on:8@12 off:4@20 on:8@24 off:5@32 on:8@37 off:4@45`. Ink runs from offset 0 rather than from the division - the phase is anchored at the OUTER corner and the first dash straddles the division line rather than starting after it.
why_it_exists: no fixture in this project drew a dashed border at all. The renderer fitted its dashes to the centreline's length where Chrome fits the outer one - `8,4,8,4,8,4,8` against `8,5,8,6,8,5,8` on a 48-pixel edge - and nothing golden could have caught it. The rhythm rested on one renderer-level assertion that called `fitted_dash` directly, which asserts the arithmetic and says nothing about the number the renderer passes in: a test that would have passed unchanged either side of the fix.
why_anchored_to_chrome: `borders-per-edge` certified two corners while they were wrong, twice, because it was accepted from our own render. The numbers above are a browser's, so a reader can check the picture against the reference rather than against the picture.
status: TARGET, anchored to Chrome in both axes. Accept the image only when the run sequence along y=2 matches AND the column at x=100 is four inked rows deep; a picture that merely looks dashed, or one that is dashed with the right rhythm and the wrong band, is what this fixture exists to refuse.
regenerated: 2026-08-24, after the corner division stopped being applied between edges that agree. Chrome re-measured for the vertical claim rather than the image being accepted from our own render.
